name: ReCOUP
question: Do liberal postoperative activity instructions improve satisfaction after prolapse surgery compared with restricted instructions?

design.blinding: double-masked (participants and outcome assessors; counseling nurses unmasked)
design.population: Women with stage II or greater pelvic organ prolapse undergoing minimally invasive reconstructive surgery at two academic centers.
design.locator: Primary report, Materials and Methods and Results; 108 enrolled, 95 allocated and assessed at 3 months

verdictNote: The prespecified satisfaction advantage was not detected; satisfaction was high in both groups.
takeaway: After reconstructive prolapse surgery, liberal activity instructions versus three months of heavy-lifting and strenuous-exercise restrictions yielded 3-month satisfaction of 44/45 (97.8%) versus 47/50 (94.0%); the superiority comparison was not significant (P = .619).

reports.label: 3-month primary report
reports.citation: Mueller MG, Lewicky-Gaupp C, Collins SA, et al. "Activity Restriction Recommendations and Outcomes After Reconstructive Pelvic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2017;129(4):608-614. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000001924
reports.followUpLocator: Primary report, Materials and Methods, primary outcome paragraph

results.measure: Completely or mostly satisfied at 3 months; odds ratio for restricted versus liberal instructions
results.note: The report's multiplicity threshold was P < .03; odds-ratio direction follows the published 0.36 estimate.
results.locator: Primary report, Results; publisher Table 4 image OCR, satisfaction row

results.measure: 3-month Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory total score, mean ± SD; lower is less distress
results.note: Secondary symptom measure; the article reports less urinary and prolapse symptom bother with liberal instructions.
results.locator: Primary report, publisher Table 4 image OCR, PFDI total row; Results

results.measure: POP-Q stage 0 or I at 3 months
results.note: Anatomic outcomes were secondary; the article reports better posterior wall support in the liberal group.
results.locator: Primary report, publisher Table 4 image OCR, 3-month POP-Q stage 0/I row; Results

harms.label: Intraoperative complications
harms.locator: Primary report, publisher Table 3 image OCR, intraoperative complications row
harms.note: The publisher table does not classify the complication types or grades.

delivery.label: Activity instructions

values.exp: Resume activity at own pace, with no lifting or high-impact restriction
values.ctl: Avoid lifting over 10 lb and high-impact activity for 12 weeks

delivery.locator: Primary report, Materials and Methods; publisher Table 1 image OCR
delivery.note: Both groups received identical advice on walking and stairs and avoided vaginal intercourse, tampons, and douching for 6 weeks.

delivery.label: Minimally invasive sacrocolpopexy
delivery.locator: Primary report, publisher Table 3 image OCR, surgical details
delivery.note: 58/95 (61.1%) overall; other operations were vaginal suspension, colpocleisis, and one abdominal sacrocolpopexy.

delivery.label: Concomitant procedures
delivery.value: Hysterectomy in 67/95 (70.5%) and incontinence surgery in 47/95 (49.5%).
delivery.locator: Primary report, Results; publisher Table 3 image OCR

delivery.label: Analyzed primary endpoint
delivery.value: 95/108 enrolled women received allocation and completed the 3-month primary outcome.
delivery.locator: Primary report, Results and Figure 1 caption
delivery.note: The arm counts describe the 95 analyzed women, not all 108 enrolled women.

reports.label: Planned 1-year analysis
reports.citation: Mueller MG, Collins SA, Lewicky-Gaupp C, et al. "Restricted Convalescence Following Urogynecologic Procedures: 1-Year Outcomes From a Randomized Controlled Study." *Female Pelvic Med Reconstr Surg.* 2021;27(2):e336-e341. doi:10.1097/SPV.0000000000000922
reports.followUp: 1 year after surgery; 83/95 functional and 77/95 functional plus anatomic assessments

results.measure: Completely or mostly satisfied at 1 year among women with functional assessment
results.note: Table 3 gives P = .238, while Results prose gives P = .155; neither meets the report's P < .03 threshold.
results.locator: 1-year report, Table 3, satisfaction row; Results prose

results.measure: Prolapse beyond hymen, apical descent over one third of vaginal length, or prolapse retreatment at 1 year
results.note: Complete anatomic assessment was available for 77/95 women.
results.locator: 1-year report, Materials and Methods; Table 4, composite failure row

results.measure: Revision surgery by 1 year among women with complete anatomic assessment
results.note: Revision operations included sacrocolpopexies and one posterior colporrhaphy.

delivery.label: 1-year assessment retention
delivery.value: 83/95 (87%) completed a functional assessment; 77/95 (81%) completed functional and anatomic assessments.
delivery.note: Complete functional and anatomic assessments: 34/45 liberal and 43/50 restricted.
